text: The answer changed every airliner that came after. Openings got rounded corners, so the stress can flow smoothly around them. The Comet came back as the Comet four, with thicker skin and rounded windows. Designers added straps that stop a crack from running, so one crack can't tear open the whole cabin. And new airliners are tested by flexing a full airframe for far more flights than they will ever fly. Today, airliner windows are small and rounded, and the skin around each one is made thicker, to carry the load around the hole. In nineteen fifty-eight, a Comet four flew the first transatlantic jet service with passengers. So the next time you look out of a round plane window, that curve is a lesson, learned the hard way. What other everyday shape do you think hides a story like this? Tell me in the comments.
